terms.meaning: the PowerPoint file format that the renderer writes
the library used to write PowerPoint files
a colour written as six letters or digits, such as CC0000 for red
a transparency value written into a colour; it must not appear here

used_by: other deck builders (not all visible in this packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Slide size and margins
sections.what: Sets the slide to widescreen, about 13.3 by 7.5 inches, with a margin of about a third of an inch and a usable content width that follows from them.
sections.why: The header says the default slide size is wrong for this deck, so all slides must use this size.
sections.watch_out: Positions outside the slide are written into the file without any warning, so a wrong position is not caught.

sections.name: PALETTE
sections.title: Colour palette
sections.what: Lists the colours for main text, muted text, the red accent, the soft accent, lines, white and the paper background.
sections.why: One list of colours keeps the deck consistent across every slide.
sections.watch_out: Each colour must be six hex characters with no hash and no alpha, or the file breaks.

sections.name: FONTS
sections.title: Font choices and text sizes
sections.what: Sets the title and body font to Arial and lists the size for each text role. It also records a title minimum of 16 points.
sections.why: One size table keeps text consistent on every slide.
sections.watch_out: The title minimum is only a convention, and the comment refers to Calibri while the font is Arial, so the real behaviour may differ.

sections.name: LEGACY_SIZES
sections.title: Older sizes still in use
sections.what: Lists sizes for appendix titles, subtitles, appendix body text and footnotes, kept from an older version of the slides.
sections.why: Kept so older slide designs still look the same.
sections.watch_out: These sizes sit outside the main size table, so changing the main table does not change them.

sections.name: LAYOUT
sections.title: Fixed positions and sizes for slides
sections.what: Holds the fixed positions, heights and sizes for slide parts such as the title, bullet list, footnote and footer. Slide builders read these numbers instead of typing their own, so the whole deck lines up the same way.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps all layout geometry in one place so a change happens in one file.
sections.watch_out: Footnote and bullet positions depend on each other, so moving one can make text overlap or run past the bottom of the slide.

sections.name: TEXT_METRICS
sections.title: Text measuring settings for line counting
sections.what: Holds the numbers used to estimate how many lines of text fit in a box: line height, space taken by the bullet symbol, a safety fraction of box width, and a fallback character width.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the pagination code predict wrapping without rendering the slide first.
sections.watch_out: If the font or line height changes, these values must change too, or text may overflow its box.

sections.name: CLASSIFICATION_COLORS
sections.title: Colours for the four verdict labels
sections.what: Gives each verdict label (cautionary tale, success story, mixed success, to be determined) a fixed colour code used on slides.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the labels themselves.
sections.watch_out: Colours are stored without a hash sign, so any code that uses them directly must add one.

sections.name: applyLayout
sections.title: Setting the slide size to widescreen
sections.what: Switches the presentation to the widescreen layout that every slide uses.
sections.why: The code comment says it must run on a fresh presentation before any slide is added.
sections.watch_out: Calling it after slides exist breaks the layout order the comment requires.

summary: Holds the single set of layout, colour, font and size values that the lessons-learnt PowerPoint renderer uses.
purpose: Keeps the look of the deck in one place so builders cannot drift apart.
why: The header says no colour, font or size may appear anywhere else in the renderer.
how: Sets the widescreen slide size and margins, then lists the colours, the font choice, the text sizes, the older sizes still in use, the layout positions, text metrics and classification colours, and a function that applies the layout to a presentation. Only the first four groups are visible in this packet.
inputs: None. This file is constants only.
outputs: Named constants that other deck files import.
risks: A hex value with a hash or alpha digits corrupts the file. The title size floor is a convention, not something the code enforces. The comment mentions Calibri while the font is Arial.
debug: If text looks too big or too small, check the font size values here. If the file will not open in PowerPoint, check the colour values for hashes or extra digits. If slides look shifted, check that the layout is applied before any slide is added.
